summary.units: Seconds relative to scheduled onset unless the field names a difference; cores are raw adjacent counter slope, not PromQL rate.
summary.clear_increment_rule: First post-onset adjacent CPU counter difference whose slope / observed 0.2-core CPU request exceeds 55 percent.
summary.window_scope: Each successful raw response finishing before scale-write start, with its own evaluation_time_unix > onset; full labels retained for calculation; source times in (evaluation-window, evaluation]. Counts describe visible source-sample availability, not a measured 30-second PromQL rate failure probability.

independent_comparison.method: Independent audit JSON and raw NDJSON compared with primary JSON output only; no primary analyzer implementation read or imported.
independent_comparison.numeric_tolerance: math.isclose with rel_tol=1e-12, abs_tol=1e-6; identity/timestamp key sets compare exact float values.

sha256_manifests.counting_unit: Verification entries, including repeated files across manifests; not unique files or independent runs.

delivery_manifests.counting_unit: Verification entries, including repeated files across manifests; not unique files or independent runs.

interpretation_limits: All ten retained runs are included in their original separate cohorts: six offsets and four cadence runs.
Only source observations completed strictly before the first successful upward Scale write started are used for pre-scale metric analysis.
Clear increment means the first adjacent raw counter slope / observed 0.2-core request > 55%; it is not a short-window PromQL rate.
Unknown visibility lower bounds remain null. Arrows in the figure indicate unknown extent, not a zero lower bound.
Raw counter, one-minute expression and controller queries are separate non-atomic observations. Their signed response-time differences are descriptive, not causal contributions.
Millisecond negative differences from concurrent queries are retained in the summary; plot rounding and vertical marker offsets do not imply negative latency.
Thirty/sixty-second window counts describe visible raw sample availability, not measured short-window query failure probabilities or service benefits.
No new load experiment was performed. cAdvisor, scrape, ingestion components and short-window closed-loop service outcomes remain unisolated.
